title: Instruments played and taking up tuba in Chicago
summary: He lists his instruments and explains studying tuba with a Chicago Symphony player around 27-28 and doubling with Buddy Fisher.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, uh, I can't play much of anything anymore, but I did play fiddle and mandolin, guitar, bass, piano, drum.
You never fooled with any wind?
No, bass, no. No, I tried to.

Oh, I played tuba, oh yeah. Well, you see, when I played tuba, I went about it right. It had to be that way because, uh, I, uh, I studied with Hamburg, tuba player, and Hamburg was second base in the Chicago Symphony, under stock. So, uh.
Well, how old were you when you took up the tuba?
Oh, I guess that would be about 27, 28.
You were already on the road, though.

Oh, yes. Well, you see, that was in Chicago. Uh-huh. That was the time when, uh, when the bands were using tuba. So I figured they weren't using much bass fiddles anymore, and that it let, well, it reduced the feel down to only a few chances of playing. So before they did, before they came to the climax, I was ready. I went to Hamburg and I bought myself a tuba, and I started taking lessons from him, and naturally I knew all the music and everything. The only thing I had to worry about was the keys and the lip, pressure on the lip to make the different tones, you know. The rest of it I could read. Well, in a short while I was playing with Buddy Fisher, playing both tuba and string bass, and for which I was compensated with additional money, doubling money. Uh-huh. But I was still in Chicago? Oh, yeah.
